title.narrative: Generation G - Rwanda

description.narrative: The Generation G partnership strives towards the creation of gender-just and violence-free societies with and for young people in their full diversity. The partnership raises public support, advocates for improved policies and laws, and strengthens civil society, all as a way to contribute to gender justice. The partnership addresses three key interrelated challenges: gender-based violence, the unequal division of care, and women’s lack of access to civic space. The Generation G partnership is a collaboration of partners in Indonesia, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Rwanda, South Africa, and Uganda, with a global consortium consisting of Rutgers (lead), ABAAD, Promundo and Sonke Gender Justice.

# of laws blocked, adopted or improved to promote womens economic rights, empowerment and entrepreneurship

comment.narrative: The baseline value is set to 0 as this indicator measures changes implemented by the programme during its lifetime.
The target for the 5 year period can be found under 2021.

In 2023, a new Law (Law 27/2023 of 18/05/2023) regulating labour in Rwanda amended the previous one of 2018, in which male employees used to have the right to 4 days of fully paid �circumstantial leave�. The Law used paternity leave for the first time but the length of the leave was not specified and the publication of a Ministerial order was awaited for it.The Ministerial Order (MO) was finally published in August, to complement the Law, and the 3 additional days were added, for a total of 7 days. This result is far from what RWAMREC and RCSP had been advocating for (a full month) but represents a partial move in the right direction.
This target is for the whole programme period: Rwanda: Law N� 68/2018 of 30/08/2018 Determining Offences and Penalties in General
